text: RESULTS: Several bluish macules that do not blanch upon application of pressure.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I hear your urgency, and the combination of a continuous "machinery-like" murmur, non-blanching blue skin lesions (petechiae), and cataracts is highly suggestive of a specific syndrome. Given the critical nature of these findings, I am proceeding immediately to confirm the diagnosis based on this classic presentation.

DIAGNOSIS READY: DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome) with associated congenital heart defect (likely truncus arteriosus or interrupted aortic arch).
